channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: 'Like we had a war': France left reeling after nationwide violent protests
item.description: France on Sunday is dealing with the aftermath of nationwide protests that damaged around 1,500 businesses and caused losses estimated at hundreds of millions of euros. Police arrested an estimated 1,800 people across the country during Saturday's demonstrations over the cost of living and school conditions.

item.title: The week in pictures: Escalating protests across Europe and the tragic capsize of a migrant boat
item.description: From student protests and heightened tensions across French demonstrations on October 17, to ongoing anti-government marches in Albania and the tragic sinking of a migrant boat off the coast of Djibouti, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.

item.title: 'Like we had a war': France counts cost of violent protests
item.description: France was reeling on Sunday from widespread damage caused by violent protests the day before that saw 1,800 people arrested, a historic town hall torched and widespread looting.

item.title: France protests: "There's a whole range of grievances at play"
item.description: Is the anger in France driven more by declining living standards or by the perception that the economic burden is being distributed unfairly? We discuss this with our guest, Joseph Downing, senior lecturer in politics and international relations at Aston University.

item.title: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties.

item.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Saint Petersburg kills one, sets refinery ablaze
item.description: A large-scale Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's second-largest city Saint Petersburg killed at least one person and hospitalised another five on Sunday. The attack – which also sparked fires at an oil refinery and depot – comes as Kyiv accused Russia of violating Washington's "energy ceasefire" dozens of times.

item.title: If you have the scratch, they have the scares
item.description: Scary stories are more than fun, they're big business.

item.title: Paris protests: A look at the aftermath
item.description: Following yesterday's demonstrations in Paris, where violent clashes erupted between police and protesters, our reporter Antonia Kerrigan returns to place de la République.

item.title: Atlanta’s iconic tavern marks Georgia’s past with an eye on future as midterms approach
item.description: Since it was established in 1956, Manuel’s Tavern in Atlanta has hosted legendary Democratic leaders while its founder played a key role in the city’s move from a Republican to Democratic stronghold. With the state’s Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff leading the polls in the midterms amid rumours of a future presidential run, the tavern is once more at the heart of the political action.

item.title: Out-of-control truck kills 13 at Hindu festival in India
item.description: A speeding truck in India killed 13 people when it ploughed into a crowd at a Hindu festival, officials said on Sunday, with President Droupadi Murmu describing the deaths as "heartbreaking".

item.title: Ukraine targets Russia with more than 1,000 drones, striking oil terminal
item.description: Russian officials said oil facilities were struck in the massive attack.

item.title: Riots in Tirana enter a fifth day as Albania's anti-government protests escalate
item.description: Clashes broke out near the Albanian prime minister’s office in the capital, Tirana, on Saturday as anti-government riots entered a fifth day.

item.title: Pope makes public appearance a day after discharge from hospital following cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo has said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties, as he greeted crowds in St Peter's Square during his first public event following lung cancer surgery.

item.title: France: Protests "brought the entire population together for a common purpose"
item.description: This weekend, in cities across France, some 800,000 protesters, including students, railway workers and members of the Yellow Vest movement, took to the streets in largely peaceful nationwide demonstrations. Sparked by a month of high school student protests over educational inequality and crumbling school facilities, the movement has grown into a broader outcry over the cost of living, public spending and climate inaction, as people across France say they have reached their breaking point.

item.title: France: Who took part in Saturday's protests?
item.description: Weeks of student protests over poor conditions in schools and rising anger over the cost of living fuelled calls for a nationwide demonstration on October 17, bringing together youth activists and supporters of the Yellow Vest movement. The main grievance was the cost of living. The protesters demonstrating against it 'didn't get what they wanted', analyses France 24's Shirli Sitbon.

item.title: France: Who was behind the violence at Saturday's protests?
item.description: Violent clashes, fires, vandalism and looting marred demonstrations across France on Saturday as hundreds of thousands of people marched against the rising cost of living and poor conditions in schools. The French Interior Ministry said about 400 people were arrested nationwide. Our partner TV station France 2 examined who was involved in the violence during Saturday's protests.

item.title: France protests: Did the government make the wrong decisions?
item.description: Police in Paris said Sunday they had arrested a "record" 855 people over protest-related violence in the capital the day before, with the prosecutor's office saying more than 500 were being held in custody. France 24's Shirli Sitbon analyses.

item.title: PSG back on top of Ligue 1 after stunning Strasbourg comeback
item.description: After trailing Strasbourg for more than 60 minutes, the Parisians called upon their substitutes to turn the game around. Following their spectacular Champions League victory over Manchester City and ahead of their clash with FC Barcelona, PSG are brimming with confidence.

item.title: Gun pictured at scene after police officer shot - as suspects hunted
item.description: A police officer has been shot in Nottingham city centre.

item.title: Major fire breaks out in Alberta after deadly incident at military base
item.description: Canada’s defense minister says that people have been killed and injured in an incident at a military base in Alberta that caused a major fire, while reports said that large numbers of injured people were being transported to hospitals

item.title: Months-long Indonesia wildfires spew toxic haze across Southeast Asia
item.description: Parts of southern Southeast Asia have been put under the highest-level haze alert as wildfires that have swept Indonesia for months continue to belch toxic smoke across the region. The seasonal wildfires are worse this year due to the drought conditions caused by a severe "super-El Nino" effect.

item.title: Woman drives truck through soccer pitch, killing child and man
item.description: Two people, including a child, were killed and 10 others injured when a woman drove a truck through a soccer field in Kansas, US police said.

item.title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder released from police custody
item.description: Indian police released Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke from detention on Saturday after the activist was detained ahead of a rally calling for the resignation of India's chief election commissioner. Two other CJP leaders remain in custody after having been arrested while demonstrating at a protest site that police had ruled off-limits.

item.title: 2 dead, 11 injured after Kansas mother drives onto soccer field during game: Police
item.description: A child and an adult were killed after a vehicle drove through a soccer game in Wichita, Kansas Saturday afternoon, police said.

item.title: Dems lead GOP in House vote choice as Trump's approval rating hits record low: Poll
item.description: Half or more Americans call every household purchase category measured "unaffordable."

item.title: Live: Trump says 'France is burning', blames 'immigration' for nationwide protests
item.description: US President Donald Trump said "France is burning" on Sunday via his social media platform Truth Social after demonstrations swept across the country over the weekend. France’s Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that police had arrested more than 1,800 people as outbursts of arson and looting broke out on the margins of peaceful marches. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Rubio says Trump to 'analyze' global impact of Russia sanctions during pause
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sanctions and tariffs on Russia would last 60 days, as the move drew bipartisan criticism and raised fears in Ukraine that Washington could ease further restrictions on Moscow.

item.title: ‘Standing up for democracy’: Atlanta ‘No Kings’ rally draws Trump critics ahead of midterms
item.description: “No Kings, Vote Now” was the theme of a rally in Atlanta, one of many organised across the US on Saturday. While many demonstrators denounced US President Donald Trump’s policies, organisers said the rally was aimed at getting out the vote in the November 3 midterm elections and protecting democracy in America.

item.title: Looters seize on massive French protests to raid and vandalise shops
item.description: Looters on Saturday seized the opportunity to raid and vandalise a host of shops and businesses across France – from bakeries and supermarkets to tech stores – as hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets to protest higher living costs and other grievances.

item.title: Crush at religious festival kills at least 17 and injures dozens in India
item.description: At least 17 people have died and dozens more are injured after a crush at a religious festival in India, local media reports.

item.title: US condemns 'despicable' Israeli settler attack that seriously injured American photographer
item.description: The US ambassador to Israel has condemned an attack by dozens of masked Israeli settlers on a village's harvest in the West Bank that left several people injured including an American photographer.

item.title: India: Police crack down on New Delhi protests
item.description: Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, ‌who was detained on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday.

item.title: More NHS staff sacked after accessing medical records of Nottingham attack victims
item.description: A total of 15 NHS staff have now been sacked after accessing medical records belonging to the victims of the 2023 Nottingham attack.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery
item.description: The Pope left Rome's Gemelli Hospital Saturday, days after surgery for lung cancer removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He is currently scheduled to travel to Latin America in November.

item.title: WATCH: David's Bridal puppy collection
item.description: Wedding retailer David’s Bridal is unveiling its new Puppy Love collection, revealing what the best-dressed best friend will wear at a pet parent’s wedding.

item.title: Zelenskyy urges support for new US sanctions on Russia after Trump puts them on hold
item.description: Zelenskyy described the move as unfortunate, adding it would encourage Russia to continue its assault. Trump told Congress that the pause was in the national interest but gave no further details.

item.title: Man and woman charged with assault and criminal damage after fatal house fire
item.description: A man and a woman have been charged with assault and criminal damage after a fatal house fire in Waterford, Ireland, that killed four members of the same family.

item.title: Dubois retains WBO title with crushing win over British rival
item.description: Daniel Dubois has retained his WBO world title after beating Fabio Wardley in their rematch at the O2 Arena.

item.title: Katie Zacharia 'transitioning out' of press secretary role, sources tell ABC News
item.description: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is “transitioning out” of her role, multiple sources and a senior White House official told ABC News on Friday.

item.title: Perspective: Midterm money madness
item.description: Campaign ad spending has topped $10 billion this election cycle, as voters struggle to afford groceries and gas.

item.title: Iran live updates: Trump admin prepares options, including 'mother of all bombs'
item.description: A dozen people were killed Saturday during a "brutal" attack at the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said.

item.title: UK advises against all but essential travel to Saudi Arabia
item.description: The UK has advised against all but essential travel to Saudi Arabia after attacks by Yemen's Houthis in the region.

item.title: WATCH: Rhode Island farmer sets new record for world's biggest pumpkin
item.description: David Muir reports on the new world record for heaviest pumpkin, which weighs 3,156 pounds – smashing the previous record of 2,856 pounds set merely a week ago.

item.title: Three men sentenced to more than 158 years in jail for murders of surfers​
item.description: Three men have been sentenced to 158 years and nine months each for the murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend.

item.title: Trump administration threatens to prosecute local California election workers
item.description: The DOJ sued over claims the state hasn't purge noncitizens from voter rolls.

item.title: WATCH: Authorities: Fatal alligator attack in Winter Garden, Florida
item.description: Police say the man was fishing along the shoreline at a park when he was attacked and killed by an alligator.

item.title: WATCH: Hero who stopped Oregon elementary school shooting suspect identified
item.description: ABC News contributor Don Mihalek discusses the bystander credited with stopping the suspected gunman and ongoing investigations.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: How Elon Musk is bankrolling GOP’s hopes in Texas Senate race
item.description: New campaign finance filings show the major role billionaire Elon Musk is playing in bankrolling GOP efforts against Democrat James Talarico in Texas.

item.title: New York Democrats want parking lot owners to ban ICE from their properties
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and top New York Democrats are urging private parking lot owners to block federal immigration officers from using their properties

item.title: WATCH: Nat Geo's 'Moment on the Earth' spotlights the wonders of elephants
item.description: National Geographic shares a closer look at elephants, including how they can eat up to 18 hours a day and even use their trunks to "hug." "Secrets of the Elephants" is streaming now.

item.title: Trump administration accused of fast-tracking migrant children's asylum cases
item.description: Immigrant advocacy groups have sued the Trump administration to stop what they call a "cruel and unlawful scheme" to fast-track migrant children's asylum cases.

item.title: WATCH: Aboard USS George Washington as tensions rise in the Middle East
item.description: ABC News is aboard the USS George Washington near the Strait of Hormuz with rare front-line access as President Donald Trump weighs expanded operations against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

item.title: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia says she did not pass bar exam
item.description: Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer; Trump called her "an attorney."

item.title: WATCH: Elon Musk unveils Tesla's new Roadster, and it can fly
item.description: Using SpaceX rocket technology, the sports car climbed a curved ramp and hurled itself to a controlled landing.

item.title: WATCH: Seahawks, Broncos face off in Thursday night NFL matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Omar Ruiz previews the Seahawks-Broncos showdown in Denver, including how Seattle’s top-ranked defense could challenge Bo Nix and whether Sam Darnold can bounce back after two interceptions.

item.title: WATCH: Rising number of young adults living with parents
item.description: ABC News’ Juju Chang reports on the growing trend of “boomerang kids” returning to live with their parents amid housing costs and financial concerns.

item.title: WATCH: DIY Halloween costumes for this year’s viral trends
item.description: Lori Bergamotto shares easy, last-minute DIY Halloween costume ideas inspired by the people and pop culture moments that made headlines this year.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir hears from Georgia firefighters who helped deliver 15 puppies
item.description: Firefighters in Cobb County answered an emergency call to help a veterinary hospital deliver 15 puppies after a rescue dog came to the local animal hospital.

item.title: WATCH: Aggressive great white shark seen off Southern California coast
item.description: Experts say the shark could be hunting for seals.

item.title: WATCH: How to navigate rising prices this holiday season
item.description: ABC News’ Elizabeth Schulze reports on what to know about the latest inflation report and prices this coming holiday season.
